title: "Before You Begin: Setup"

::: {.callout-note}
### Session at a Glance

**Total core time: about 30 minutes**, most of it waiting for packages
to install.

| Section | Time | Type |
|---|---|---|
| What you will install | 10 min | Hands-on |
| Get the course repository | 5 min | Hands-on |
| Restore the course library | 10 min | Hands-on |
| Check you are ready | 5 min | Hands-on |

Do this once. Everything else in the course assumes it is done.
:::

## What You Will Install

Four tools, in this order. If you already have one, skip it.

| Tool | Why | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **R** (4.4.0 or later) | The language everything is written in | [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org) |
| **RStudio** or **Positron** | An IDE. Either works; the course shows RStudio | [posit.co/downloads](https://posit.co/downloads/) |
| **Quarto** | Renders the book and runs the code chunks | [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) |
| **Git** | Gets you the repository and its history | [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/downloads) |

::: {.callout-warning}
### Windows: install Rtools too

On Windows, install **Rtools44** to match R 4.4.x, from
[cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).
Without it, any package that needs compiling will fail to install, and
the error message will not obviously say why.

macOS and Linux users do not need this step.
:::

## Why This Course Pins Its Packages

In regulated clinical work, "it worked on my machine" is not a defence.
A submission has to be reproducible years after it was built, by
somebody who is not you, on a machine that does not exist yet. That is
not a nice-to-have. It is what the whole apparatus of standards,
define.xml and reviewer guides exists to support.

So this course practises what it teaches. It uses
[**renv**](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) to record the exact version
of every package it depends on in a file called `renv.lock`. When you
restore that lockfile, you get the same package versions the author had,
not whatever CRAN is serving today.

`renv.lock` is a teaching artifact, not overhead. It is the smallest
honest example of the thing the rest of the course is about: **a result
you can hand to someone else and have them reproduce exactly.**

## Get the Course Repository

Clone it, or download it as a ZIP from
[github.com/sufyansuleman/cdisc-with-r](https://github.com/sufyansuleman/cdisc-with-r).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sufyansuleman/cdisc-with-r.git
cd cdisc-with-r
```

Then open **`cdisc-with-r.Rproj`** in RStudio. This matters more than it
looks: opening the project sets R's working directory to the project
root, which is what every code chunk in the course assumes. Paths in the
sessions are written as `data/sdtm/dm.csv`, not
`../data/sdtm/dm.csv`. They only resolve if you are at the root.

If you use Positron or run R from a terminal, `cd` to the repository
root before starting R, and confirm with:

```r
getwd()   # should end in /cdisc-with-r
```

## Restore the Course Library

Opening the project runs `.Rprofile`, which activates renv and points
your session at [Posit Public Package
Manager](https://packagemanager.posit.co/) for precompiled binaries.
You will usually see renv announce itself, and often a note that the
library is out of sync, that is expected on a fresh clone.

Run this once, in the R console at the project root:

```r
renv::restore()
```

renv lists what it is about to install and asks you to confirm. Say yes.

**What to expect.** Several minutes, and a lot of output. Binaries make
this fast on Windows and macOS by default, and on Linux via the
`__linux__/jammy` P3M repository the `.Rprofile` selects. If it starts
compiling packages from source and crawling, that is the signal
something is off with the repository configuration rather than with
you. See the troubleshooting section below.

A successful restore ends quietly, with no error, and:

```r
renv::status()
#> No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```

That message is the goal. If you get anything else, fix it here rather
than discovering it three sessions in.

## Check You Are Ready

Run this snippet. It loads what the course loads, reads a file the way
the sessions read files, and checks the controlled-terminology package
can answer a question:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(sdtm.terminology)

# 1. the data ships with the repo. This should print 401 rows
dm_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/dm_raw.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(dm_raw)

# 2. controlled terminology is available
ct("list") |> dplyr::filter(term == "SEX")

# 3. Quarto is on your PATH
Sys.which("quarto")
```

You are ready when all three run without error: the read returns **401
rows** (yes, 401, 400 subjects and one duplicate enrolment, which you
will meet in [Why Standards](why-standards.qmd)), the codelist lookup
returns the `SEX` codelist `C66731`, and `Sys.which()` returns a path
rather than an empty string.

To confirm the whole book builds, run this in a terminal at the project
root:

```bash
quarto render
```

## If Something Went Wrong

**`renv::restore()` fails on Windows, mentioning compilation.**
Rtools44 is missing or does not match your R version. Install it, restart
R, try again.

**Packages compile from source and take forever.** Check that
`.Rprofile` ran - `getOption("repos")` should show a
`packagemanager.posit.co` entry. If it does not, you probably opened R
somewhere other than the project root.

**`renv::restore()` reports nothing to do, but `library(tidyverse)`
then fails.** The lockfile and your library disagree. Run
`renv::status()` first and read what it says before installing anything
by hand, that message is the diagnosis.

**A code chunk says it cannot find `data/raw/dm_raw.csv`.** Your working
directory is not the project root. Run `getwd()` and, if needed, reopen
`cdisc-with-r.Rproj`.

**Everything installs but the book will not render.** Check Quarto is on
your PATH with `quarto --version` in a terminal. RStudio bundles its own
Quarto, which can differ from the one your terminal sees.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Still stuck?

Open an issue at
[github.com/sufyansuleman/cdisc-with-r/issues](https://github.com/sufyansuleman/cdisc-with-r/issues)
with the output of `renv::status()` and `sessionInfo()`. Those two
together identify almost every setup problem.
:::
